platforms.name: Embraer C-390 Millennium
platforms.payload_notes: Maximum payload 26,000 kg; up to 80 troops or 74 litters.
platforms.range_notes: Ferry range approximately 6,100 km with auxiliary tanks; tactical radius approximately 1,800 km with 14 t payload.
platforms.role: Tactical and strategic airlift, troop transport, cargo (including vehicles), aerial refuelling (KC-390 variant), MEDEVAC, search and rescue
platforms.engine: 2 × International Aero Engines V2500-E5 turbofan, 31,360 lbf each
platforms.indian_relevance: Contender in the open IAF Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) competition, alongside the Lockheed Martin C-130J. The Defence Procurement Board has cleared a 60-aircraft MTA requirement, and a formal tender had not been released as of mid-2026 — the IAF has not selected a platform. Embraer's documented Indian industrial partner is Mahindra Defence (MoU February 2024 at the Embassy of Brazil, New Delhi; strategic-alliance scope deepened October 2025). No Embraer–HAL MoU exists. The programme is intended to absorb part of the An-32 replacement requirement.
platforms.indian_partner_role: Indian industrial partner under MoU (Feb 2024, deepened Oct 2025); Tier-1 supplier scope and FAL location under negotiation
platforms.indian_production_status: No production committed to India as of mid-2026. Embraer and Mahindra Defence signed a strategic-alliance MoU (Feb 2024, deepened Oct 2025) covering industrial cooperation, FAL options and MRO scope. The IAF MTA competition remains open — the C-390 is a contender, not a selected platform.
platforms.localization_summary: Industrial scope not yet contracted. Targeted levels: L1 (assembly) to L2 (component manufacturing) for structural and avionics sub-assemblies. Engine and FADEC remain L0.
platforms.localization_depth_target: L1-L2 (assembly + component manufacturing); L3 (system integration) for candidate Indian-led sub-systems — contingent on the MTA competition outcome
platforms.strategic_significance: Second major Western transport-aircraft industrial partnership opportunity in India within a decade of the C-295, should the MTA competition convert to a contract. A Mahindra-led industrial vehicle would complement the TASL-led C-295 model. First turbofan-powered transport in IAF service outside the Il-78 / A-50 derivatives. Strategic competitor to the A400M and C-130J at the global level.

platforms.payload_notes: Maximum payload 6,700 kg; 39 troops or 24 paratroopers. Hot-and-high performance was a design driver.
platforms.range_notes: Ferry range approximately 2,800 km with standard fuel.

platforms.indian_relevance: IAF operates approximately 100+ An-32s delivered from 1984 onwards. Principal tactical transport workhorse. Mid-life upgrade of 40 aircraft to An-32 RE standard performed jointly by UkrOboronProm and IAF No. 1 BRD Kanpur (2009–2018). Subsequent fleet upgrade of 50+ aircraft by IAF BRDs using Indian-supplied upgrade kits. Spare-parts supply disrupted post-2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

platforms.localization_depth_target: Steady-state — no further localisation planned; fleet to be progressively replaced by C-295 / C-390 absorption.
platforms.strategic_significance: Largest single-platform tactical transport fleet in IAF service. High-altitude / hot-and-high performance is mission-critical for Himalayan operations. Spare-parts supply from Ukraine disrupted post-2022, exposing fleet availability risk.

platforms.localization_summary: L0 — fully imported in the hypothetical Indian procurement scenario.
platforms.strategic_significance: Reference platform for the heavy-lift transport category. The A400M demonstrates the upper bound of Western transport-aircraft industrial complexity (composite primary structures, FADEC-controlled 11,000-shp turboprop, full-authority FBW). The Atlas records it as the benchmark against which any Indian heavy-lift industrial partnership would have to be calibrated.
